title: Chapter 2 Quiz 1
description: The first two families: algorithms that run in a straight line and algorithms that decide.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Which type of algorithm runs its instructions one after the other, with no decisions and no repetitions?
questions.explanation: A linear (sequential) algorithm executes step by step in a straight line, for example adding two numbers and printing the result.

questions.question: Which task suits a **linear** algorithm?
options: Adding two numbers and showing the sum
Checking whether a user's age is valid
Adding up every number in a long list
questions.explanation: A fixed sequence with no decision or repetition is linear. Watch out: checking an age needs a decision, and adding every number of a list needs a loop.

questions.question: Which type of algorithm is the best choice to **validate user input**, such as checking whether a number is positive?
questions.explanation: Conditional algorithms use branching (if-else, switch-case) to take decisions, which is what validation needs.

questions.question: A conditional algorithm uses branching such as if-else or switch-case.
questions.explanation: Branching is what makes an algorithm conditional.

questions.question: Which of these are typical uses of a **conditional** algorithm?
questions.explanation: Conditional algorithms are used when the solution depends on a condition. Watch out: adding two numbers or printing a fixed message needs no decision, so they are linear.

questions.question: A {{1}} algorithm runs in a straight line, while a {{2}} algorithm chooses between branches such as if-else.
Complete the conditional algorithm that displays whether a person is an adult (18 or older).
questions.code:
Read(age)
If age {{1}} 18 Then
    Display("Adult")
{{2}}
    Display("Minor")
EndIf
questions.explanation: Adults are 18 or older, so the condition is age >= 18. The other branch starts with Else.

questions.question: This algorithm should display Adult for a person who is 18 or older. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Read(age)
If age > 18 Then
    Display("Adult")
Else
    Display("Minor")
EndIf
questions.explanation: A person who is exactly 18 is an adult. Watch out: with age > 18, an 18-year-old would be called a Minor.
